name: PBB Maestro
shortDescription: Observer-only worker telemetry and local service health visibility for operators of a managed PBB node.
longDescription: PBB Maestro collects and presents approved health and worker telemetry so operators can see whether important local services are responding. Its confirmed role is observation, not general remote administration.

Service lifecycle actions remain with the configured Windows service and node operating procedures. Health visibility does not replace application-level validation, recovery plans, or field escalation.

readiness.note: Observer-only telemetry and health visibility are implemented for the confirmed local service set.
remainingWork: Complete alert ownership and escalation thresholds for each deployment.
Validate telemetry coverage across all pilot service configurations.
Publish troubleshooting and recovery runbooks linked to each health signal.

nodeRole: Gives authorized local operators a consolidated observer view of service and worker health without becoming an unrestricted remote-control plane.
localBehavior: Approved health signals remain visible on the managed local network.
The observer can report configured worker and service states without a cloud dashboard.
connectivityBehavior: Remote viewing is not implied and requires a separately approved secure route.
Telemetry visibility alone does not repair a failed application or service.
operationalConsiderations: Assign an owner and response procedure to every actionable signal.
Keep the monitored service inventory aligned with the actual node configuration.
securityBoundary: Maintain observer-only permissions in the publicized foundation.
Do not expose health endpoints or operational details to an untrusted network.

faqs.question: Can Maestro remotely control every service?
faqs.answer: No. Maestro watches the health of local services and workers. It is not a general tool for remotely controlling them.

faqs.question: Does local monitoring require internet access?
faqs.answer: No, as long as Maestro and the services it checks are running on the managed local network.

faqs.question: What starts and stops node services?
faqs.answer: Windows service tools and the node's documented operating procedures are responsible for starting, stopping, and restarting services.

faqs.question: Does a health warning automatically resolve an incident?
faqs.answer: No. A warning still needs an assigned person to investigate it, decide when to escalate it, and follow the approved recovery steps.

faqs.question: Is the health view publicly reachable?
faqs.answer: No. It should normally be available only to authorized operators on the managed network. Any remote access needs a separate security review and approval.
